claims: March Madness is the annual NCAA Division I men’s and women’s basketball tournament.
March Madness is a single-elimination tournament.
March Madness teams play over three weeks in March and April.
March Madness determines the US national champion.
March Madness concludes the college basketball season.
March Madness culminates in the Final Four.
ESPN notes that 68 teams compete in a single-elimination format in March Madness, meaning a single loss ends a team's season.
EBSCO states that the March Madness field of 68 is chosen and seeded by a committee.
EBSCO states that 32 March Madness teams earn automatic bids by winning conference tournaments.
EBSCO states that 36 March Madness teams receive at-large invitations.
Dummies.com explains that the March Madness tournament begins with the First Four games.
Dummies.com explains that the First Four games narrow the 68 teams down to the 64-team bracket for the first round.
NCAA.com says the phrase March Madness was first used by Henry V. Porter in 1939 to describe Illinois high school basketball.
NCAA.com says the phrase March Madness was popularized for the NCAA tournament by broadcaster Brent Musburger in the early 1980s.
Www.olympics.com states that the March Madness tournament is famous for Cinderella teams, which are lower-seeded underdog teams that make surprising deep runs in the tournament.
The March Madness tournament is held for both men's and women's Division I basketball.
The men's and women's March Madness tournaments run concurrently in the spring.
